issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Rideable' (with method messageOnRide()), but the solution implementation introduces a different interface name 'Mountable' and has classes (Pig, Seal) implementing Mountable instead of Rideable. This naming mismatch between the specification/template and the solution will confuse students about which interface to implement and can break compatibility with the provided Main/template code and tests that reference Rideable.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution's 'Mountable' interface to 'Rideable' and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable, or update the problem statement/template to use 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable'. Ensure the interface declares messageOnRide() with the expected signature and that all references (Main, UML, tests) use the same interface name.

issues.description: The solution repository contains a Rideable.java file that is empty/non-functional while the rest of the solution uses 'Mountable'. An empty Rideable.java file contradicts the problem statement (which expects a Rideable interface) and will confuse students or automated checks if they encounter this file.
issues.suggestedFix: Populate Rideable.java in the solution with the correct interface declaration (messageOnRide()) and update classes to implement it, or remove the unused Rideable.java file if 'Mountable' is the chosen name — but ensure exactly one interface with the expected name/signature exists across problem, template, and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a Rideable interface (UML and Main.java use 'Rideable'), but the solution implements the same concept under the name 'Mountable' (Mountable.java, Pig and Seal implement Mountable). This inconsistent identifier naming for the same conceptual entity (an interface providing messageOnRide()) creates mapping confusion: students comparing the UML/problem or the template starter code to the reference solution will not easily recognize that Mountable == Rideable, increasing extraneous cognitive load and risking incorrect implementations or misunderstandings.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier names so the same interface name is used everywhere. Recommended: rename the solution's Mountable interface and all its usages to Rideable (rename Mountable.java -> Rideable.java; update Pig.java and Seal.java to 'implements Rideable'), and remove the unused/empty Rideable.java file in the solution. Alternatively, update the problem/template to use 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable', but prefer Rideable to match the UML and starter code.
